questions.stemHtml: Blood supply of the marked structure in the given specimen is derived from which of the following arteries?
questions.solutionHtml:
Anterior Cerebral Artery
  • The structure marked in the Image is the fornix. It is supplied by the anterior cerebral artery.
  • The anteromedial central branches from the anterior cerebral artery supply the fornix along with optic chiasma, lamina terminalis, hypothalamus, Para-olfactory areas, and cingulate gyrus.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-1464.e62.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following nerves supplies the marked structure in the given below Image?
questions.solutionHtml:
CN 4
  • The structure marked in the Image is the superior oblique muscle. It is innervated by the Trochlear nerve.
  • All the muscles of the eyeball are supplied by oculomotor nerve except superior oblique (supplied by trochlear nerve) and lateral rectus (supplied by abducens nerve).

Extraocular muscle




Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-1464.e12

questions.stemHtml: Identify the marked structure in the given dissection specimen:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ulnar Nerve

The structure marked is the ulnar nerve.  

Ulnar nerve and ulnar artery traversing in hand

  • The ulnar nervearises from the brachial plexus. It is a continuation of the medial cord, containing fibres from spinal roots C8 and T1.
  • In the forearm, the ulnar nerve pierces the two heads of the flexor carpi ulnaris, and travels deep to the muscle, alongside the ulna.



Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-957.e1

questions.stem: Which part of the brachial plexus does not give branches?
questions.solutionHtml:
Division
  • The divisions in the brachial plexus do not give any branches
  • The roots, trunks, and cords all give out direct branches.


Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-876.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following muscle do not contribute to the marked tendon:
questions.solutionHtml:
2nd Palmar interossei
  • The structure marked in the Image is the dorsal digital expansion of the middle finger.
  • Palmar interossei do not attach to the middle finger and therefore it does not contribute to the dorsal digital expansion of the middle finger.

Dorsal digital expansion

  • An extensor expansion (dorsal expansion) is the special attachments by which the extensor tendons insert into the phalanges.
  • These flattened tendons of extensor muscles span the proximal and middle phalanges.
  • At the distal end of the metacarpal, the extensor tendon will expand to form a hood, which covers the back and sides of the head of the metacarpal and the proximal phalanx.



Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-979.

questions.answerText: Loss of sensation of tip of index finger dorsal side
questions.solutionHtml:
Loss of sensation of tip of index finger dorsal side
  • The structure marked in the Image is the median nerve in the cubital fossa. A lesion of the median nerve causes loss of sensation of the nail of the index finger as it supplies Lateral 2/3rd of palm by superficial cutaneous branch & Lateral 3 ½ fingers (palmar aspect and dorsal aspect of nail beds) by palmar digital nerves.
  • The median nerve continues in the cubital fossa medial to the brachial artery and passes between the two heads of the pronator teres, deep to the bicipital aponeurosis (aponeurosis of biceps) and superficial the brachialis muscle. It crosses the ulnar artery (branch of brachial artery) while being separated by the deep head of the pronator teres.

Median Nerve cutaneous innervation

  • It then travels between the flexor digitorum superficialis (above) and flexor digitorum profundus (below). The median nerve is accompanied by the median artery (a branch of anterior interosseous artery) during this course.
  • Then, about 5 cm above the flexor retinaculum (wrist), it emerges between the flexor digitorum superficialis (medially) and the flexor carpi radialis (laterally) into the hand.





Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-942.

questions.stemHtml: Lesion on the marked structure in the given specimen would present which of the following feature:
questions.solutionHtml:
Contralateral hemiplegia
  • The structure marked in the Image are the pyramids.
  • These are two elongated elevations, one on either side of the anterior median fissure, and are produced by the underlying corticospinal (pyramidal) fibres.
  • At the pyramids' most caudal end, the corticospinal axons decussate (or crossover) the midline and continue down the spinal cord on the contralateral side. The fibers that decussate will go down the lateral corticospinal tract while the fibers that did not decussate will travel down the anterior corticospinal tract. 

A lesion here leads to contralateral hemiplegia due to involvement of the corticospinal (pyramidal) fibres .

Pyramid of brain stem,showing crossing of lateral corticospinal tract





Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-442-445.

questions.stemHtml: The marked structure given in the specimen is derived from which embryonic derivatives:
questions.solutionHtml:
Endocardial cushion

Interventricular Septum

  • The structure marked is the membranous part of the interventricular septum that is derived from endocardial cushions.
  • Endocardial cushions are soft tissue masses that protrude in the atrioventricular and conotruncal regions.
  • Atrioventricular cushions are derived from overlying endocardial cells.
  • Upon sectioning of the heart the atrioventricular endocardial cushions can be observed in the lumen of the atrial canal as two thickenings, one on its dorsal and another on its ventral wall.
  • These thickenings will go on to fuse and remodel to eventually form the valves and septa of the mature adult heart.




Langman's Medical Embryology , 14th Edition, Page No. 194.

questions.stemHtml: All of the following are artery are supplies the marked part the specimen; except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Diagonal artery
  • The structure marked is the right ventricle, It is not supplied by the diagonal artery.
  • The diagonal artery is a branch of the anterior interventricular artery supplying the left ventricle. This is present in about 30-50% of the population.
  • The right ventricle is mostly supplied by the right coronary artery and its branches such as the marginal artery.
  • The anterior interventricular artery gives off 1-2 anterior right ventricular branches 

Coronary circulation




Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-1464.e68,1464.e69.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following viscera is related to marked area over left kidney:
questions.solutionHtml:
Stomach
  • The marked area in the Image of the left kidney is related to the stomach.
  • The upper pole of the kidney is covered by the suprarenal gland. Anteriorly, the right kidney is related to the liver, duodenum, ascending colon or right colic flexure, and small intestine.
  • The left Kidney is related to the spleen, stomach, pancreas, descending colon or left colic flexure, and small intestine.

Anterior relations of kidneys




Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-1261,1262.

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following crosses the marked structure:
questions.solutionHtml:
Pudendal Nerve
  • The structure marked is the ischial spine and pudendal nerve is related to it.
  • The pudendal nerve exits out of the pelvis by passing through the greater sciatic foramen.
  • It then enters the perineum below the pelvic floor by passing around the ischial spine. It originates from the sacral plexus S2-S4.
  • The ischial spine is used as a landmark for pudendal nerve block.

Pudendal Nerve




Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-1359.

questions.stemHtml: Identify the marked layer in the given histological section:
questions.solutionHtml:
Inner limiting layer

The layer marked is the Inner plexiform layer.

Layers from outside to inside in retina are :

  1. Retinal pigment epithelium;
  2. Rods and cones (photoreceptors);
  3. External limiting membrane;
  4. Outer nuclear layer;
  5. Outer plexiform layer;
  6. Inner nuclear layer;
  7. Inner plexiform layer;
  8. Ganglion cell layer;
  9. Nerve fiber layer;
  10. Inner limiting membrane

The retina is the innermost layer of the wall of the eye. It is in immediate contact with the vitreous cavity on one side and with the choroid (of the uveal layer) on the other side.



Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-804.

questions.stemHtml: Lesion of the marked structure leads to which of the following deformity?
questions.solutionHtml:
Wrist drop
  • The structure marked in the Image is the radial nerve demonstrated in the cubital fossa.
  • A lesion of the radial nerve leads to a wrist drop.
  • Claw hand deformity is seen in a lesion of the ulnar nerve.
  • Ape thumb deformity is seen in a lesion of the median nerve.

Cubital fossa





Gray’s Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice-42nd edition page No-942,943.
